summary: Alexander Rödel is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He earned an MSc by Research at the University of Edinburgh (~2007–2008), where he was supervised by Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw.

Alexander W. Macdonald (1923–2018) worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He held a post at the Musée de l'Homme and served as a professor at Paris Nanterre University (~1970–1993), where he taught Katia Buffetrille.

Alexander Wynne (born 1974) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Bristol under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin, and earned a DPhil at Oxford (2000–2003) supervised by Richard Gombrich.

Alexander Yiannopoulos specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and worked under supervisor Karin Myers (~2015–2017), alongside traditional teachers Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche, Khenpo Sherab Sangpo, Khenpo Sherab Dorje, and Khenpo Jampa Donden.
Alexander Zieseniss (1899–1945) was an Indologist. During his career, he held posts at Leiden University, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Breslau (~1937–1945).

Alexander von Rospatt is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. After studying at the University of London and completing his PhD at Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, he held posts at Leipzig University (~1993–2003) and UC Berkeley (~2003–present).

Alexander von Staël-Holstein (1877–1937) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Dorpat, Berlin, Halle-Wittenberg, and Harvard, later holding posts at Peking University (~1922–1929) and as director of the Sino-Indian Institute (~1928–1937).

Alexandra van der Geer is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied under Leendert A. van Daalen, Henk Bodewitz, and Paul Yves Sondaar, and has served as a funded project researcher at the International Institute for Asian Studies.
Alexandre Langlois (1788–1854) was an Indologist who studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He was a member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (~1835–1854).

Alexis Sanderson (born 1948) works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Balliol College and under Lakshman Joo, later holding posts at Merton College, Brasenose College, and Oxford, including as Professor at All Souls College (~1992–2015).

Alf Hiltebeitel (1942–2023) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. Educated at Haverford College (~1959–1963) and the University of Chicago (~1964–1973), he served as Professor of Religion at George Washington University from ~1968 to 2021.
Alfons Fürst (born 1961) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tübingen until 1915 and held a post at the University of Münster in ~2006.

Alfonsa Ferrari (1918–1954) was a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome under Giuseppe Tucci and Carlo Formichi (~1936–1941), continuing there in post-graduate research from ~1941 until 1954.

Alfred Bloom (1926–2017) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. After studying at Penn, Andover Newton, and Harvard (PhD ~1963), he held posts at Harvard, served as Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies, and was Emeritus Professor at Hawaii.

Alfred Cooper Woolner (1878–1936) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Ipswich School and Trinity College, Oxford. He served as Principal of Oriental College, Lahore (~1903–1928), and as Vice-Chancellor of the University of the Punjab (~1928–1936).

Alfred Foucher (1865–1952) was a scholar of Indology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the École Normale Supérieure, he held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1900–1914) and the University of Paris (~1907–1936).
Alfred Gell (1945–1997) studied at the London School of Economics and Political Science (~1968–1971) and later held an academic post there from ~1979 to 1997.

Alfred Hillebrandt (1853–1927) was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler (~1871–1875) and at the University of Munich (~1875–1876), later serving as professor at the University of Breslau (~1883–1921).

Alfred Ludwig (1832–1912) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Vienna and Berlin. After completing his habilitation at the University of Vienna in 1858, he served as a professor at Charles University from 1860 to 1912.
Alice Y. Tseng specializes in Japanology and history/archaeology. She studied under Eugene Y. Wang (~1998–2004) and has served as a professor at Boston University since ~2004.
